primary_reviews.rationale: The genre tag names the child-local form well: a two-verse superscription ('Yahweh...spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying, Speak to the children of Israel', 1:1-2) fused with the first case-protasis ('If his offering is a burnt offering from the herd', 1:3). I probed whether all three animal-class cases in ch.1 (herd/flock/bird) ought to collapse into one chunk on the strength of the 3:6-16 lamb/goat precedent, and found the analogy points the other way: ch.1's herd/flock split mirrors ch.3's herd-vs-flock top-level division (3:1-5 vs 3:6-16), not the finer sub-merge inside ch.3's flock case, because each animal-class case here carries its own complete closing formula the way ch.3's herd case does. Severing 1:1-2 as a standalone superscription -- the alternative the writer names -- has nothing but bare instruction with no case content, so folding it into the first case it introduces is the stronger reading.

primary_reviews.rationale: The label 'grain_offering_torah_cooked_cases_and_general_rule' is honest about being a compound, but the compound is where the trouble sits. Verses 4-10 (oven/griddle/pan protases sharing one presentation apodosis at vv.8-10) genuinely earn a case-series merge in the spirit of 3:6-16. Verses 11-13 do not belong in that series: they are a second-person, negatively-phrased statute ('No meal offering which you shall offer to Yahweh shall be made with yeast...Every offering of your meal offering you shall season with salt', vv.11,13) that openly claims jurisdiction over 'every offering of your meal offering' -- meaning the raw case at 2:1-3 (M8-Lev-004) too, not merely the cooked cases it is bundled with here. The 2.10/2.11 line that the decision declines to draw is exactly the kind of seam this book marks by peeling a generalizing coda off the specific torah it follows -- see M8-Lev-009 (3:17, a one-verse second-person statute split off from 3:1-16), M8-Lev-027 (7:7-10, a cross-offering generalization split off from 7:1-6), and M8-Lev-060 (11:41-45, a generalizing prohibition-plus-motive-clause split off from the swarming-creatures list). Measured against that pattern, folding 2:11-13 into the cooked-case series is the outlier. The most coherent regrouping is either splitting at 2.10/2.11 -- a case-series chunk (2:4-10) plus a standalone coda (2:11-13) -- or going further and pulling 2:1-10 (raw+cooked, all sharing the bring-present-burn-allocate shape) into one case-series chunk with 2:11-13 standing alone; either satisfies the 'prefer the larger coherent unit' instruction better than a grouping that lets a coda outgrow the case series it is attached to. The decision's own named alternative -- a four-way split by cooking method plus a separate coda -- is a straw man built to be rejected; it never weighs the alternative that actually holds up, treating 2:11-13 as its own coda while leaving the case-series intact or enlarged.

primary_reviews.rationale: The seam itself survives inspection: 2:11 opens כָּל הַמִּנְחָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר תַּקְרִ֨יבוּ֙ לַיהוָ֔ה לֹ֥א תֵעָשֶׂ֖ה חָמֵ֑ץ with a fronted כָּל-scoped subject and 2mp verbs (תַּקְרִ֨יבוּ֙, תַקְטִ֧ירוּ), and the end at v.13 is corroborated twice over -- a setumah after 2:13 and v.14's own fresh protasis וְאִם תַּקְרִ֛יב מִנְחַ֥ת בִּכּוּרִ֖ים. The defect is in the stated evidence basis, not the placement. The rationale rests the whole boundary on 'a clean addressee-frame break from the 3rd-person cooked-case protases of vv.4-10', and a direct check of WLC falsifies that description: 2:4 is וְכִ֥י תַקְרִ֛ב (2ms), 2:5 and 2:7 read קָרְבָּנֶ֑ךָ (2ms suffix), 2:6 וְיָצַקְתָּ֥ עָלֶ֖יהָ שָׁ֑מֶן and 2:8 וְהֵבֵאתָ֣ are 2ms weqatal. What actually happens at v.11 is a number shift inside the second person, 2ms to 2mp -- a real signal in this book, but a materially weaker one than the addressee change the record claims. Compounding it, the 2mp register the rationale makes definitional runs only through v.12: v.13 reverts to 2ms throughout (מִנְחָתְךָ֮, תִּמְלָח֒, מִנְחָתֶ֑ךָ, קָרְבָּנְךָ֖, תַּקְרִ֥יב), so the unit is not register-uniform and its own second evidence ref quotes the 2ms verse as if it evidenced the 2mp claim. This is the same defect class the boss corrected at 21:1-6, where a stated 'unbroken second-person plural sweep' failed a direct check; it is filed here because the record as frozen asserts a person-register the Hebrew contradicts and cites a 2ms clause as proof of a 2mp frame. primary_reviews.rationale: 'Perpetual_statute_coda' names it right: a one-verse, second-person-plural generalizing statute stands apart in genre from the third-person casuistic material it closes. The addressee shift is unmistakable -- v.17 swaps 'he'/'his offering' (vv.1-16) for 'you...your generations...your dwellings' ('It shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings, that you shall eat neither fat nor blood'), a clean, textbook discourse-frame shift that counts as strong evidence on its own even with no fresh speech formula backing it up. Keeping this apart from the goat case (3:12-16) is right despite the thinness of a single verse, because the addressee change outweighs mere proximity. It's also a useful yardstick for M8-Lev-005 (2:11-13): this decision shows the writer knows how to peel a second-person generalizing statute off preceding case law once the addressee shifts, which makes skipping that move at 2:10/2:11 look more like an oversight than a considered call.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: OL's challenge disputed. Verified oshb Lev.3.17 חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם בְּכֹל מוֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶם כָּל חֵלֶב וְכָל דָּם לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ -- לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ is genuinely 2mp, a clean, unambiguous shift from the 3rd-person casuistic voice running through 3:1-16 ('he shall offer,' 'he shall lay his hand,' etc.). That addressee-frame shift is real, tier-1 evidence for a boundary independent of any paragraph marker. OL's parallel to MT Lev.6.11 (= WEB 6:18) does not hold up under direct check: verified oshb Lev.6.11 כָּל זָכָר בִּבְנֵי אַהֲרֹן יֹאכֲלֶנָּה חָק עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם -- יֹאכֲלֶנָּה is 3ms ('every male... he/it shall eat it'), NOT 2mp. The 'eternal statute' idiom recurs there, but the addressee does not shift to 2nd person the way it does at 3:17; OL's claim that 'the same formula class' sits non-severed at 6:11 overstates the parallel, since the actual diagnostic signal (addressee shift) is absent at 6:11. OL's marker claim (petuchah after 3:17, none after 3:16) is unverifiable from the supplied oshb file, which carries no paragraph-marker annotations, and per the evidence rules a marker claim alone would be insufficient regardless. OL's third leg -- that M8-Lev-005 refuses an analogous split at 2:11-13 -- is factually accurate and a genuine inconsistency in the draft (see my M8-Lev-005 entry, where I support LF's parallel challenge), but the better resolution is to bring 2:11-13 into line with 3:17's treatment, not to erase 3:17's well-evidenced boundary. Net: the challenge correctly spots an inconsistency but proposes the wrong-direction fix.

primary_reviews.rationale: The merge is right and better supported than the record states. WLC 4:1 וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר plus 4:2 דַּבֵּ֞ר אֶל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֘ל לֵאמֹר֒ נֶ֗פֶשׁ כִּֽי תֶחֱטָ֤א בִשְׁגָגָה֙ is a superscription-plus-general-condition, and 4:3 אִ֣ם הַכֹּהֵ֧ן הַמָּשִׁ֛יחַ יֶחֱטָ֖א is the first offender-class im-protasis under it. The two cited parallels verify exactly: 1:2 דַּבֵּ֞ר ... אָדָ֗ם כִּֽי יַקְרִ֥יב followed by 1:3 אִם עֹלָ֤ה קָרְבָּנוֹ֙, and 7:11 וְזֹ֥את תּוֹרַ֖ת זֶ֣בַח הַשְּׁלָמִ֑ים followed by 7:12 אִ֣ם עַל תּוֹדָה֮ -- so the draft's inconsistency the revision names is real. Independent corroboration the record does not claim: OSHB places no paragraph marker at 4:2|3 anywhere, and places a petuchah after 4:12, so the MT paragraph runs 4:1-12 and closes precisely where this row closes -- strong corroboration of the end, and consistent with (though not proof of) the merge at the front. The end is also on a positive signal: 4:13 opens the congregation case with וְאִ֨ם כָּל עֲדַ֤ת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יִשְׁגּ֔וּ. No defect within +/-3 verses; nothing is orphaned by folding 4:1-2 forward because the general condition's scope over the three later cases is a matter of the text's own logic, not of chunk membership. Dispositioned: the three evidence refs are bare ranges with no Hebrew quoted, unlike this cluster's normal practice, and the rationale's inline quotation is unpointed consonantal text; both are accurate, but the row would be stronger with pointed quotations from 4:2 and 4:3 and with the 4:12 petuchah added.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: SPOT 6 (part 3 of 3). No formal challenge, but OL flags a confidence-inversion worth independent assessment: draft rates 'low,' OL says this is 'among the best-corroborated boundaries in the cluster.' I find this claim overstated relative to the other two confidence-inversion flags (M8-Lev-015, M8-Lev-037). Verified the list-formula opening at 11:29 (וזה לכם הטמא בשרץ השרץ על הארץ) genuinely parallels 11:2/11:9/11:13's openings -- real tier-1 evidence for the START boundary. But OL's cited corroboration for the boundary is a setumah, which the evidence rules explicitly classify as weak (unlike petuchah, 'strong corroboration'), so 'best-corroborated' overstates what a setumah alone contributes. More importantly, the draft's actual stated ground for its 'low' rating was NOT boundary-placement uncertainty at 11:28/29 or 11:38/39 (both reasonably well-marked by fresh list-formula/protasis) -- it was uncertainty about the INTERNAL cohesion call of keeping vv.29-30 merged with vv.31-38 rather than splitting bare-list from contamination-rules the way birds (055) were split from insects (056). That internal-cohesion question is genuinely a closer call (the pronoun back-reference at v.31 supports the merge, but so would a parallel-structure argument favor a split, as the draft itself flags in its own strongest_rejected_alternative), and rating it 'low' is defensible on that specific, narrower axis even though the outer boundaries are solid. Net: the calibration critique is only partially sound here -- it correctly flags that the outer boundaries are stronger than 'low' would suggest, but it conflates that with the internal-cohesion judgment, which is the actual, still-legitimate source of the low rating, and overstates the setumah's evidentiary weight in the process.

primary_reviews.rationale: The colophon is real and quoted correctly: WLC 12:7 ends זֹ֤את תּוֹרַת֙ הַיֹּלֶ֔דֶת לַזָּכָ֖ר א֥וֹ לַנְּקֵבָֽה, and its לַזָּכָ֖ר א֥וֹ לַנְּקֵבָֽה explicitly names both halves of what precedes -- the male timeline of vv.2-4 and the female timeline of v.5 -- so it genuinely brackets the sex-differentiated material together with the offering procedure of vv.6-7. The internal seam the merge overrides is correctly characterised as weak: 12:6 opens וּבִמְלֹ֣את יְמֵ֣י טָהֳרָ֗הּ לְבֵן֮ א֣וֹ לְבַת֒, a be-plus-infinitive-construct temporal transition that itself refers back to both cases, not a fresh casuistic protasis. The close is on a positive signal as well: 12:8 opens וְאִם לֹ֨א תִמְצָ֣א יָדָהּ֮ דֵּ֣י שֶׂה֒, a genuine poverty-alternative protasis. The distinguishing 7:11ff precedent holds -- 7:12 אִ֣ם עַל תּוֹדָה֮, 7:16 וְאִם נֶ֣דֶר א֣וֹ נְדָבָ֗ה, 7:18 וְאִ֣ם הֵאָכֹ֣ל יֵ֠אָכֵל, 7:21 וְנֶ֜פֶשׁ כִּֽי תִגַּ֣ע are all fresh openers. Two dispositioned observations. First, the cited 7:19 is not a protasis: וְהַבָּשָׂ֞ר אֲשֶׁר יִגַּ֤ע בְּכָל טָמֵא֙ is a fronted-subject clause with a relative, so that one ref overstates the class it is offered for; 7:12/7:16/7:18/7:21 carry the point without it. Second, the rationale argues that the 12:6 seam 'is uncorroborated by any MT paragraph marker anywhere in the chapter'. I verified the factual claim -- ch.12's only OSHB marker is a petuchah after 12:8 -- but under the campaign's own weighting absence is never counter-evidence, and that same absence applies symmetrically to the chosen close at 12:7. The clause should be struck as an argument; the colophon alone carries the merge, and does so sufficiently.

primary_reviews.rationale: The Wiederaufnahme record is exact, and I checked it word by word. 16:6 reads וְהִקְרִ֧יב אַהֲרֹ֛ן אֶת פַּ֥ר הַחַטָּ֖את אֲשֶׁר ל֑וֹ וְכִפֶּ֥ר בַּעֲד֖וֹ וּבְעַ֥ד בֵּיתֽוֹ; 16:11 repeats that clause consonant for consonant, וְהִקְרִ֨יב אַהֲרֹ֜ן אֶת פַּ֤ר הַֽחַטָּאת֙ אֲשֶׁר ל֔וֹ וְכִפֶּ֥ר בַּֽעֲד֖וֹ וּבְעַ֣ד בֵּית֑וֹ, and then advances the action with new content the summary had only announced, וְשָׁחַ֛ט אֶת פַּ֥ר הַֽחַטָּ֖את אֲשֶׁר לֽוֹ. That is verbatim resumption plus continuation, the diagnostic signature of resumptive repetition rather than a fresh unit-opening, and the bracketed digression is genuinely required by the procedure: the lot-casting of vv.7-10 must precede v.15 for שְׂעִ֤יר הַֽחַטָּאת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָעָ֔ם to be identifiable at all. The real seam the row relocates to v.15 is verified and is the strongest kind: a new sacrificial object in explicit contrast, אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָעָ֔ם against the twice-stated אֲשֶׁר לוֹ of vv.6 and 11, with atonement scope widening at v.16 from the kapporet to הַקֹּ֗דֶשׁ, אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד and the altar. No defect within +/-3 verses: v.14 ends a complete blood-sprinkling clause and v.15 opens with a finite verb of its own. Dispositioned: the row argues its internal seam and its close thoroughly but never argues its own start at 16:6, which was inherited unchanged by the merge. The only signal there is the re-naming of the explicit subject אַהֲרֹן at the pivot from provisioning (16:3-5) to rite, and OSHB has no marker anywhere inside ch.16 to corroborate it. That start is defensible but thin, and is not a defect this revision introduced.

primary_reviews.rationale: The claimed start at 18:6 is sound, a 2mp general heading (ish ish el-kol-she'er besaro lo tiqrevu legallot ervah) with a setumah after v.6 confirming it stands apart. The challenge is to the span's extent. The ervat-X-lo-tegalleh formula runs continuously and without exception from 18:7 to 18:17, eleven verses each opening with construct ervat plus relative plus lo tegalleh/tegalleh. WLC 18:18 breaks it: ve'ishshah el-achotah lo tiqqach litsror legallot ervatah aleiha bechayyeiha. Verse 18 is not ervat-fronted and its verb is tiqqach, not tegalleh; it instead matches the following block exactly, waw plus fronted prepositional or object phrase plus lo plus 2ms verb, which is the shared shape of 18:18 (ve'ishshah el), 18:19 (ve'el ishshah), 18:20 (ve'el eshet), 18:21 (umizzar'acha), 18:22 (ve'et zachar) and 18:23 (uvechol behemah). The rationale asserts 'thirteen kinship-based sexual prohibitions, every one sharing the identical ervat-X-lo-tegalleh formula', and verse 18, inside the claimed span, does not share that formula. Since the span's unity is claimed on formula identity and formula identity fails at its last verse, the boundary is one verse late.

primary_reviews.rationale: CONFIRMED: the eight cases are kept whole, which is the answer to the campaign brief's question, and the terminating signal at v.17 is real, WLC shifting from mot yumat to venichretu / avono yissa / aririm. Splitting the list per-offence would fragment a genuine register whose members share one penalty apodosis and differ only in the offence named. The rationale states the span is 'eight casuistic protases, each opened with ve'ish asher ... and closed with the identical mot yumat apodosis'. Against WLC: (1) v.9 opens ki ish ish asher, not ve'ish asher; (2) v.16 opens ve'ishshah asher, not ve'ish asher; (3) v.14's apodosis is ba'esh yisrefu oto ve'ethen, not mot yumat. Six of eight openers and seven of eight apodoses match; the two openers that do not are precisely the first and last verses of the span, i.e. the two the uniformity claim is being used to fix. Verdict is 'supports' because the span is right and the v.17 signal holds independently, burning still being a capital penalty and vv.9 and 16 still being casuistic-plus-death-sentence members, but the claim should be restated as a capital-penalty register with formula variation at its edges rather than as formal identity.

primary_reviews.rationale: The claimed start at 21:1 is sound: a speech formula with a class-restricted addressee, and note the rarer vayyomer rather than vayedabber. The challenge is to the span's extent and to the reasoning that produced it. The rationale rejects the v.5 split on the ground that vv.1-6 are 'addressed in one unbroken second-person plural sweep without a new protasis or addressee marking a break between them.' Both halves of that claim are false against WLC. First, vv.1-6 are not second person at all: every finite verb is third person, the second-person forms in the chapter being the ve'amarta of the v.1 speech frame and the veqiddashto of v.8, both outside vv.2-6. Second, the sweep is not unbroken: vv.1-4 are uniformly 3ms (lo yittamma at v.1, lah yittamma at v.3, lo yittamma at v.4) and vv.5-6 are uniformly 3mp (lo yiqrechu, lo yegallechu, lo yisretu, qedoshim yihyu, velo yechallelu). The number shift falls exactly at the candidate seam the writer names and rejects, and it coincides with the topic change from corpse defilement to mourning disfigurement. The stated reason for merging therefore asserts the absence of precisely the signal that is present. On corroboration I am explicit: OSHB places a setumah after 21:9 and nothing before it, so the Masoretic paragraphing groups 21:1-9 as one unit and does NOT corroborate my proposed split; setumah is tier-3 weak and marker absence is not counter-evidence, but I record that it does not help me. I note in mitigation that the writer's own 21:6|21:7 seam is equally unmarked, so declining to split at v.5 for want of a marker while splitting at v.7 would be inconsistent.

primary_reviews.rationale: The narrowing is correct on every point I could test. The span opens on a fresh divine-speech formula with an addressee specification, 21:1 וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֱמֹ֥ר אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים בְּנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֑ן וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם. The 3ms claim verifies across the whole span: לְנֶ֥פֶשׁ לֹֽא יִטַּמָּ֖א בְּעַמָּֽיו (v.1), לָ֖הּ יִטַּמָּֽא (v.3), לֹ֥א יִטַּמָּ֖א בַּ֣עַל בְּעַמָּ֑יו לְהֵ֖חַלּֽוֹ (v.4) -- and vv.2-3's relative-exception list hangs on v.1's verb, so cutting anywhere earlier than v.4 would sever a protasis chain. The register shift at v.5 verifies as 3mp and marks the close. Nothing within +/-3 verses is orphaned or subjectless. Dispositioned, and worth carrying forward: the first verb at 21:5 is a ketiv/qere pair -- ketiv יקרחה, qere יִקְרְח֤וּ -- and the evidence ref quotes the qere without tagging it as such. The 3mp identification does not depend on that word: וּפְאַ֥ת זְקָנָ֖ם לֹ֣א יְגַלֵּ֑חוּ, וּבִ֨בְשָׂרָ֔ם לֹ֥א יִשְׂרְט֖וּ, and the 3mp suffixes בְּרֹאשָׁ֔ם / זְקָנָ֖ם / בִבְשָׂרָ֔ם are all unambiguous, so the shift stands on the rest of the verse regardless of which reading is adopted. Also dispositioned: OSHB places no marker at 21:4|5, so paragraph evidence is neutral; the person register carries it alone, which is legitimate under the campaign's weighting.

primary_reviews.rationale: The front of this span is sound. 21:5 opens the 3mp block (לֹ֣א יְגַלֵּ֑חוּ, לֹ֥א יִשְׂרְט֖וּ, with 3mp suffixes throughout), v.6 continues it (קְדֹשִׁ֤ים יִהְיוּ֙ לֵאלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם וְלֹ֣א יְחַלְּל֔וּ), and the row is right that v.7 does not break it: אִשָּׁ֨ה זֹנָ֤ה וַחֲלָלָה֙ לֹ֣א יִקָּ֔חוּ ... לֹ֣א יִקָּ֑חוּ is the same register with no protasis or addressee change at the 6|7 seam, so the absorption of the narrowed 21:5-6 tail is justified and the rejected alternative it names is correctly rejected. The defect is at the other end. The span's stated defining property is that it 'is uniformly 3mp', and its own last verse is not: 21:8 is second person from its first word -- וְקִדַּשְׁתּ֔וֹ, כִּֽי אֶת לֶ֥חֶם אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ ה֣וּא מַקְרִ֑יב, קָדֹשׁ֙ יִֽהְיֶה לָּ֔ךְ, closing on מְקַדִּשְׁכֶֽם. That is not 'a single embedded 2ms/2mp aside at v.8b'; it is the entire verse, in a different person from the block it is attached to, spoken to a different addressee (the lay Israelite, as the row itself concedes) from the priests addressed at v.1. The verified 3mp register runs 21:5-7 and stops there, with v.7 closing on its own כִּֽי קָדֹ֥שׁ ה֖וּא לֵאלֹהָֽיו. The rejected-alternative field considers only stopping at v.6 and never confronts the 7|8 seam at all. What makes this challengeable rather than a matter of taste is internal inconsistency across this very revision set: at 24:15 an addressee redirect is the decisive splitter (M8-Lev-149 / M8-Lev-150), and at 15:31 a bare person-and-scope shift earns a standalone one-verse row (M8-Lev-183). Absorbing an addressee change silently here, inside a unit defined by register uniformity, repeats in kind the defect the boss corrected at 21:1-6, where a stated person-register failed a direct check. OSHB places no marker at 21:7|8 or 21:8|9, so paragraph evidence is neutral and cannot settle it either way.

The finite verbs of the block run third-person plural without interruption: v.5 לֹא יְגַלֵּחוּ ... לֹא יִשְׂרְטוּ שָׂרָטֶת; v.6 קְדֹשִׁים יִהְיוּ לֵאלֹהֵיהֶם וְלֹא יְחַלְּלוּ ... הֵם מַקְרִיבִם וְהָיוּ קֹדֶשׁ; v.7 לֹא יִקָּחוּ ... לֹא יִקָּחוּ. The ketiv/qere handling is exact: Lev.xml carries ketiv יקרחה with rdg type=x-qere יִקְרְחוּ, and plural reference is secured independently of that variant by the three 3mp pronominal suffixes inside the same verse, בְּרֹאשָׁם / זְקָנָם / וּבִבְשָׂרָם -- a firmer warrant than the record's appeal to later verbs alone, and worth adding. Two precision corrections that do not disturb the span. (a) 'uniformly 3mp throughout' overstates the tail of v.7, whose motive clause is a distributive third-person SINGULAR, כִּי קָדֹשׁ הוּא לֵאלֹהָיו; third person is uniform across 5-7, 3mp is not. The record quotes that clause separately, so the claim is transparent rather than concealed, but the adjective should be softened to 'third person throughout, 3mp in all finite prohibitions'. (b) The row's left edge at 4|5 is neither cited nor characterised anywhere in the record, although a real signal supports it: 21:1-4 is third-person SINGULAR throughout (לְנֶפֶשׁ לֹא יִטַּמָּא v.1, לָהּ יִטַּמָּא v.3, לֹא יִטַּמָּא בַּעַל בְּעַמָּיו v.4) and v.5 switches to plural, exactly where the neighbouring row M8-Lev-126 (Lev.21.1-21.4) ends. That is a NUMBER shift inside the third person, not a person shift, so the seam is genuine but must not be labelled a person seam; the record should cite it rather than inherit the edge silently. The load-bearing 7|8 seam holds: no element of 5-7 is second person, while every clause of v.8 carries a second-person morpheme. It gains corroboration the record does not cite -- v.8's first motive clause is a person-switched doublet of v.6's, כִּי אֶת אִשֵּׁי יְהוָה לֶחֶם אֱלֹהֵיהֶם הֵם מַקְרִיבִם (v.6) against כִּי אֶת לֶחֶם אֱלֹהֶיךָ הוּא מַקְרִיב (v.8): the same rationale formula re-aimed at a different addressee, which tells for the split rather than the merge. The overruled-differentiator record is honest: v.9 does read בָּאֵשׁ תִּשָּׂרֵף and v.8 carries no penalty, so the abandoned sanction-clause theory's factual predicate is stated correctly before being declined; and penalty language is equally absent from the 21:1-4 and 21:5-7 rows, so it could not have been the operative criterion. Paragraph facts verified and correctly non-driving: Lev.xml has x-pe after Lev.20.27, x-samekh after Lev.21.9, x-pe after Lev.21.15, and no marker at 4|5, 6|7, 7|8 or 8|9; the record calls this neutral rather than reading absence as counter-evidence, and no marker functions as a driver. One tagging nit: the third evidence ref, 'oshb:Lev.21.8 (2nd person throughout ...)', quotes no Hebrew and restates M8-Lev-189's datum -- it is the same single witness seen from the far side of the seam, not an independent second attestation; the '(single-witness)' tag correctly stops it reading as corroboration. Span verified; the defects are record-completeness only and do not move the boundary.

primary_reviews.rationale: Read against the five-unit map (1-4 | 5-7 | 8 | 9 | 10-15), 21:5-7 holds together as one register with no internal addressee change. It opens with paired self-disfigurement bans, 'They shall not shave their heads or shave off the corners of their beards or make any cuttings in their flesh' (v.5), grounds itself in its own motive clause, 'They shall be holy to their God, and not profane the name of their God, for they offer the offerings of Yahweh made by fire, the bread of their God. Therefore they shall be holy' (v.6), pivots to marriage restrictions, 'They shall not marry a woman who is a prostitute, or profane. A priest shall not marry a woman divorced from her husband' (v.7a), and closes on its own formula, 'for he is holy to his God' (v.7b). Nothing in that stretch shifts who is being addressed -- the priests remain the third-person subject throughout. The seam at v.8 is where the English marks a hard person shift: 'Therefore you shall sanctify him, for he offers the bread of your God' moves from 'they/their' to 'you/your' with a new addressee, confirming rather than undercutting the 7|8 boundary this decision draws. On the near side, the absorption of 5-6 from a neighboring decision's narrowed tail is not tested by this cluster and produces no seam trouble -- 1-4's corpse-defilement case (singular 'a priest ... he') and 5-7's disfigurement/marriage case (plural 'they') are both third-person, so the harder boundary in the neighborhood is correctly identified as 7|8, not 4|5. The strongest_rejected_alternative is recorded honestly: it states the prior 5-8-merge position, names the specific reasoning abandoned (treating v.9's stated penalty, 'She shall be burned with fire,' versus v.8's absence of one as the operative differentiator), and gives the textual ground for abandoning it (person and independent-clause structure, not penalty presence). That is a complete and non-self-serving record of the revision, not a strawman.

But the span's stated defining property -- 'uniformly 3mp' -- fails at its own last verse. I confirmed 21:8 is second person in every clause from its first word: וְקִדַּשְׁתּ֔וֹ (2ms verb), כִּֽי אֶת לֶ֥חֶם אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ (2ms suffix), קָדֹשׁ֙ יִֽהְיֶה לָּ֔ךְ (2ms/2fs dative), closing on מְקַדִּשְׁכֶֽם (2mp suffix). The verified 3mp register runs 21:5-7 and closes on v.7's own כִּֽי קָדֹ֥שׁ ה֖וּא לֵאלֹהָֽיו; the row's rejected-alternative field never confronts the 7|8 seam, only a stop at v.6. primary_reviews.rationale: Checked fresh against OSHB Lev.21.8-9. Every second-person morpheme the record labels checks out: וְקִדַּשְׁתּוֹ (2ms weqatal with 3ms object suffix), כִּי אֶת לֶחֶם אֱלֹהֶיךָ (2ms suffix), קָדֹשׁ יִהְיֶה לָּךְ (לָּךְ is the pausal 2ms under zaqef qaton, not 2fs), כִּי קָדוֹשׁ אֲנִי יְהוָה מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם (2mp suffix) -- and the record itself flags the 2ms-to-2mp widening, which is honest reporting rather than smoothing. Two qualifications on the description, neither fatal. First, 'second person in every clause from its first word' is accurate as a claim about DEIXIS -- each of the four clauses carries a second-person morpheme -- but three clauses have third- or first-person grammatical SUBJECTS (הוּא מַקְרִיב, יִהְיֶה, אֲנִי יְהוָה); the enumerated parentheticals keep a careful reader from being misled, but the headline must not be read as 'wholly second person'. Second, 'two independent כי clauses' is loose: both כי clauses are grammatically subordinate causal clauses. What is actually independent is the pair of MAIN clauses, וְקִדַּשְׁתּוֹ and קָדֹשׁ יִהְיֶה לָּךְ, each carrying its own כי motive. The substantive point survives the correction and is the right one: v.8 is a complete command-plus-rationale in its own right (imperatival weqatal, its ground, a consequent state, its ground), not a motive tail hanging off vv.5-7, so the standalone unit reads coherently on its own two כי clauses. The addressee gloss 'the lay Israelite' is an inference past the bare signal: the 2ms could instead resume the Moses-address frame of 21:1 (אֱמֹר אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים ... וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם), which is the strongest reading the record does not engage. But מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם is plural and cannot be Moses alone, and on either reading the addressee is not the priests spoken ABOUT in 3mp in vv.5-7, so the 7|8 seam stands whichever referent is chosen; the gloss should be marked as interpretation, not as the evidence. The 8|9 seam holds on three converging signals: v.9 opens a fresh casuistic protasis with a new subject and a different FUNCTION for כי -- וּבַת אִישׁ כֹּהֵן כִּי תֵחֵל לִזְנוֹת (conditional כי, 3fs תֵחֵל), apodosis אֶת אָבִיהָ הִיא מְחַלֶּלֶת בָּאֵשׁ תִּשָּׂרֵף (3fs throughout) -- against v.8's two causal כי clauses, and the final row set gives v.9 its own row (M8-Lev-186). Both consistency appeals verified against the book's own final rows and TRUE of the current set: Lev.15.31 stands as a standalone one-verse row, M8-Lev-183 (וְהִזַּרְתֶּם אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, 2mp weqatal breaking out of the third-person prescription of 15:29-30), and the 24:15 addressee redirect is a live boundary, M8-Lev-149 (Lev.24.13-24.14) against M8-Lev-150 (Lev.24.15-24.22) opening at וְאֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל תְּדַבֵּר לֵאמֹר. Both Hebrew quotations in the refs are exact. Caveat for the record: earlier freeze snapshots carried 15:28-31 and 24:13-16 merged, so the parentheticals are true of the current row set and should not be read as describing every prior snapshot. primary_reviews.rationale: V.8 reads as a complete, doubly-grounded command in its own right: 'Therefore you shall sanctify him, for he offers the bread of your God. He shall be holy to you, for I Yahweh, who sanctify you, am holy.' Both 'for' clauses are independent grounds for the two second-person commands ('you shall sanctify him' / 'he shall be holy to you'); the verse is not a dependent tail hanging off v.7's third-person motive clause, 'for he is holy to his God' -- that clause belongs to the 5-7 register and its addressee, while v.8 pivots to a different addressee (the community being told how to treat the priest) using 'you/your' throughout. Isolating v.8 does not orphan it: 'him' anaphorically resumes 'priest,' a referent established at v.1 and carried through 5-7, and a forward-linked-but-grammatically-distinct one-verse unit is exactly the pattern already visible elsewhere in the English text at the cited precedents. Lev.15:31, 'Thus you shall separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, so they will not die in their uncleanness when they defile my tabernacle that is among them,' stands as its own single-verse unit even though 'their uncleanness' depends on the discharge case-list before it -- the same anaphoric-but-severable pattern claimed for 21:8. Lev.24:15, 'You shall speak to the children of Israel, saying, Whoever curses his God shall bear his sin,' marks a fresh unit at a bare addressee-redirect with no paragraph break at that seam at all, which is the right analogue for treating person/addressee shift as decisive independent of paragraphing. On the far side, v.9, 'The daughter of any priest, if she profanes herself by playing the prostitute, she profanes her father. She shall be burned with fire,' is a fresh third-person-feminine case with its own subject and its own stated penalty, independently confirming the 8|9 seam. The label 'priest_sanctification_duty_command' fits the content: a command (sanctify him) grounded in duty language (he offers the bread of your God) and a second self-predicating divine motive, addressed past the priest to the people.

OL's two grammatical refinements both hold up under independent re-checking, not just re-reading: (1) three of the four clauses have third- or first-person grammatical SUBJECTS despite second-person deixis -- הוּא מַקְרִיב (3ms subject), יִהְיֶה (3ms subject, referring back to the priest), אֲנִי יְהוָה (1cs subject) -- so 'second person in every clause' is accurate only as a claim about deixis/morphemes present, not about grammatical subject, and OL's qualification is a fair, verifiable correction that does not touch the boundary. primary_reviews.rationale: The book-final colophon, and the Hebrew citation in the decision is accurate to the source. אֵלֶּה הַמִּצְוֺת אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהוָה אֶת מֹשֶׁה אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּהַר סִינָי is the same deictic-plus-category-plus-locative construction as 26:46, differing only in naming one category (הַמִּצְוֺת) where 26:46 names three, and it closes the בְּהַר סִינַי frame that runs 25:1, 26:46, 27:34. Its scope is retrospective and cannot be tithe law, so separating it from vv.30-33 is right and 'high' is warranted. Treating this colophon as its own chunk is also the treatment I argue should have been applied to 23:37-38.
